events.title: Mount Fuji Erupts for the Last Time
events.description: Mount Fuji began its Hōei eruption, which sent ash across the region and blanketed Edo (now Tokyo) in fine volcanic dust. The eruption lasted about two weeks and created a new crater on the mountain's flank.
events.significance: It is the most recent eruption of Japan's tallest and best-known volcano, which has been quiet ever since.

events.title: The Boston Tea Party
events.description: Colonists, some disguised as Mohawk men, boarded three ships in Boston Harbor. They dumped 342 chests of British East India Company tea into the water to protest taxation without representation.
events.significance: Britain answered with the punitive Coercive Acts, which pushed the colonies toward the American Revolution.

events.title: The Battle of the Bulge Begins
events.description: Germany launched a surprise offensive through the Ardennes forest in Belgium and Luxembourg. It hit thinly held Allied lines in freezing winter weather.
events.significance: It was Germany's last major offensive on the Western Front. Its failure drained the army's remaining reserves and hastened the end of World War II in Europe.

events.title: Pakistani Forces Surrender in Dhaka
events.description: Pakistani forces in East Pakistan surrendered to the joint forces of India and Bangladesh. This ended the Bangladesh Liberation War after nine months of conflict.
events.significance: The surrender led to the birth of Bangladesh as an independent nation. The country marks the day every year as Victory Day.
